raw_response:
I will keep my land mainly in the usual wheat-maize rotation, because that fits Quzhou County best, matches my experience, and spreads my risk across the whole year. I know winter wheat grows steadily here if I topdress in spring and water at the key stages, and summer maize follows well after wheat harvest with reliable demand and easier field management. I do not want to scatter my effort across too many crops, because that raises labor, management mistakes, and sales uncertainty. I will use improved seed for wheat and hybrid seed for maize, put most of my fertilizer into the base and key growth periods, irrigate only when it matters most, and keep pesticide sprays limited to real disease and insect pressure. For tillage, I will rotary-till after harvest because it is practical, fast, and works with the machines I can get. My goal is steady yield and stable cash flow, not chasing the highest possible output with the highest cost.
